utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Mr. Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. As we planned yesterday, we will spend about a few minutes on the motion for the judicial notice. Ms. Chana, are you in the position to tell us the Prosecution's position on that motion filed by Defence?

utterances.speaker: MS. CHANA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good morning. The Prosecution does come bearing a solution to this, Your Honour. What we propose and we have sent to the Defence this morning, the annex A and the annex B to the judicial -- to their adjudicated fact motion and we have put in italics and we give Your Honours a copy, of what we are prepared to agree to, Your Honour. We are not going to -- we do not think the facts as posed by the Defence are suitable for adjudicated facts, but the Prosecution is prepared to -- by agreement to agree on the facts which we have put in italics there. Your Honour, there is nothing to preclude this Chamber under Rule 65 ter (H) at the trial phase to do them by agreement, to the extent that no evidence needs to be led by the Defence on the facts that we agree to. Your Honours, they are not capable of being considered adjudicated facts, these are two Trial Judgments, Your Honour, they are not on appeal, and one of the purposes of adjudicated facts is to achieve consistency at the appellate level, and I think the solution is that we agree to the facts, and most of those facts are the ones which are factual finding of the court as opposed to a lot of those facts which are just a retention of the -- of the evidence of the witnesses which I don't think are capable of being considered adjudicated facts. So I have isolated those facts which are findings of the court and I think for the purposes of the Defence, they will be more than adequate and I think this is a sensible solution to this -- the proposal as put forward by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any response? Yes, Mr. Mettraux?

utterances.speaker: MR. METTRAUX
utterances.text: Yes, good morning, Your Honour. As the Prosecution has indicated we received a what seems to be a -- if you want, a counterproposal to our original proposal and we are quite happy with the idea submitted by the Prosecution. I mean, we think that the facts in question would be and could be regarded as adjudicated fact but the solution suggested by our colleague seems to satisfactory indeed. We haven't had the time to go through the whole document carefully but if given some time during the day, we think that we could just sit with the Prosecution and find a solution which would avoid the Chamber having to rule on this issue and I think that the fact identified by the Prosecution are indeed those which the Defence was most interested in having agreed upon or adjudicated upon. So given some time during the day we can certainly find a solution, we believe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much indeed. Of course we will give the Defence sometime to go over those facts. And as for how do we regard those facts, I believe it's just a matter of the formalities, and whether it could be regarded as adjudicated facts or not is another matter but the facts are there. If the parties agree with those facts, we don't care about whether it's -- has already been adjudicated or not. But the other matter is that the motion filed by Defence on the 1st of March, which has been on the table for a long time, and we are very sorry that we haven't got any response during that long period. But anyway, we will see whether we could make a ruling on those facts before the recess. I don't think it's wise for us to leave it further along. Yes, are there any other matters that the parties would like too raise? It seems to me, none. Could we have the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Did you have a good rest yesterday?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You are not satisfied with your stay in The Hague. Well, we will try our best to let you go home at this weekend, but I cannot promise you anything at this stage. We will do our best. Are you ready to start?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I had to change my hotel last night so that's why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry. I'm sorry to hear that. Yes, Mr. Re, are you ready?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just about.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There was one thing from yesterday -- General, good morning to you, that I over looked clarifying before one of our breaks. Could we please return to Exhibit P122? There was a question I asked yesterday before there was a break, after there had been a reasonably lengthy objection and some discussion with the Trial Chamber, and that was about the resubordination. What I was asking you was who was -- who was being resubordinated and to whom within that -- by the terms of that order?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it states in this order, the Dreznica Battalion was resubordinated to the Zulfikar Brigade, and since it's the plural here they mean all the units from the 1st Corps which arrived or are on the way, and the artillery and their crews -- its crews. And as it states here under item 3, 220-millimetre mortars, 105-millimetre howitzer, 276-millimetre cannons, 132-millimetre Howitzer, and launcher rocket system of 107 millimetres. So this is the order under which these units were resubordinated to the Zulfikar Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And on the terms of the order, is it Mr. Halilovic who is resubordinating units from the 1st Corps to the Zulfikar unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I object to that. The face of this document reveals that it's sent from Jablanica on the 6th of -- 6th of September. It appears to be directed to, if you look at the people who it's addressed to, at the back of the document it appears to be addressed to a number of corps and to Sefer Halilovic personally, to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, that will be a major issue, whether this document is Mr. Halilovic's document or is a document to him. Maybe we could make that sure first.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On the terms of the document, Mr. Karavelic, who does it appear, from what is written on the document, is doing the resubordinating and from who to who? It is a who-is-doing-what-to-who question.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to say again that amongst other things, this also is a question for a military expert. However, since these are very sensitive issues, and I'm here also involved in some way directly or indirectly, and I am stating that openly here before this Tribunal, and in my wish to be as objective as I can be, regardless of who bears how much responsibility, I can comment on that. Could I just see the bottom part of the document? I think that that's how it was, and that is that a team or a group of officers -- I wouldn't call it a forward command post or an inspection team or so on, they will -- it will be determined what that was, headed by General Sefer Halilovic, and it's a fact that at the time they were in the Neretva River valley. Of course, due to numerous various circumstances, they were not able to install and form their own separate communication centre, which, from a military point of view, was possible to do, but on the other hand, there was no need if they could use one of the existing communication centres, such as, for example, in this case, the 6th Corps communication centre. Why double the resources is the already-existing means of communication or the 6th Corps communication centre could be used for their own purposes? That is why the 6th Corps communication centre was used, of the 6th Corps Command, and all communication by General Sefer Halilovic and the members of his team, in terms of receiving and sending documents, were dispatched and received through the 6th Corps command communication centre, and this is quite logical and quite proper from a military point of view. This document, since it states here that it was sent to the Chief of Staff, Sefer Halilovic, personally, it's possible that at that time this document, I assume, since there are no initials down here who drafted the document, very few or practically no document was drafted by General Sefer Halilovic himself. It's not his job to personally draft the documents. He issues general directives and guidelines, instructions, and then, based on that, the assistants, officers, write the orders, each in his own area of responsibility, and depending on the type of combat operations and the type of activity. So the person whose duty was from the team to do so drafted this order. At that moment, Sefer Halilovic was not close by, was not there, and that's why it states here that it is also to be delivered to him personally so that he can see for himself what it says in the document and which units are mentioned and so on, because this is impossible to remember off by heart, the units, the types of weapons and so on. It's not possible to keep them all in mind, the ones that are mentioned in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Your view is that probably someone else, not General Sefer Halilovic, actually drafted this document, but in light of your experience, who does it appear on the face of this document is doing the subordinating? I mean, whose order is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'd object to that again. The document itself makes it clear and the witness's answer makes it clear and the Prosecutor is having a second try now at something he didn't get before, and I object.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I press the question because my question is a different one to the one the witness answered. The witness answered about the process. I'm asking him for an opinion as to whose order it appears to be based upon the terms of the document. He hasn't asked that -- he hasn't answered that, and it's certainly within his area of expertise as a very senior army officer to look at this document and say, well, this was whoever. It appears, I don't know but it appears within normal military doctrine to be a document of X or Y or Z. That's all I'm asking for, an opinion as to whose document or who appears to be doing the subordinating and I haven't got to that point. It's not a question of me asking a question to an answer I didn't like the answer to. I didn't get the answer at all to that particular question. So I press it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, if that's the new question then I object to it because the witness has said that he doesn't have the expertise and that it should take a proper expert who has had the chance to properly prepare and see all the documents before making -- giving such an opinion. My friend says he's plainly got the expertise. The witness appears to say that he hasn't. And I object to the witness being asked to give opinions on the run. He may be capable of having the expertise if he's given the chance, but at the moment he thinks he hasn't and the Defence thinks he hasn't and we object accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that the witness has already answered the question. Of course there is some problems concerning this document and there are different views between the two parties. The next work will leave to the Bench's judgement. We will consider the document as well as the testimony of this witness and we'll come to a conclusion on that. Mr. Re, would you please skip this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I please move to document P270.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry to trouble the Prosecutor here but my eyes are missing the 65 ter number of that. Could I just inquire what that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I'm grateful, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's a document dated the 25th of September 1993, under the letterhead of the 2nd Independent Motorised Battalion. It's addressed to the 1st Corps Command, is a report from the field for the period of 7th of September to the 20th of September and is signed by Zakir Okovic and Adnan Solakovic. Have a look at this document, you said yesterday you needed assistance with looking at documents to remind you of the dates of the return from the field of the various units, including this one. Have you seen or do you remember seeing this document in 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does reading this document assist you on the dates of the dispatch of the 2nd Independent Battalion to Jablanica and their return from the field?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It states in the document that they left on the 8th of September That's what it says on the -- in the second passage in this document. And then at the end of the document, it says that they returned the last day, that was the 19th or the 20th of September 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to question the accuracy of those dates?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the other two brigades? That's the 9th and the 10th. What can you say about the time when they departed in respect to the -- in relation to the dates in this document, which is the 8th of September 1993, when it says the 2nd went to Jablanica. When did the 9th and the 10th go? Was it the same time or days earlier or days later?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid that I could make a mistake. It's hard to remember all the dates but I think that those two companies from the 9th and the 10th Brigades left a few days before this unit from the 2nd Independent Battalion, and that also they returned - I think, but I'm not sure; we would need to check the documents - that they returned to Sarajevo a little later, after the units from the 2nd Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, did you issue -- did you issue orders to parts of the 9th and the 10th to return to Herzegovina later that month, after they had returned to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need to check my orders issued after General Sefer Halilovic issued the order of the 23rd of September to form the new unit from the battalion which I was supposed to send down there. I don't -- to see whether a unit from the 10th Mountain Brigade was a part of that or not. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What do you mean you would need to check your orders?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To see in the orders which units were part of this new unit, this battalion, so that I could send it there, in accordance with the orders of the 23rd of September by the order by General Sefer Halilovic, as I said. I don't know just like that, off the top of my head, which units I used in order to form this new battalion. I don't know which -- the brigades that these companies came from. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you looked in your orders, that would tell you, would it?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where would we find these orders, Mr. Karavelic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the archives of the federation of the army -- of the Army of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And when was the last time you saw copies of these orders, Mr. Karavelic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did see them. I can't say when. Recently, recently. Often parts of documents -- I have actually copies of some documents in my own personal archive.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, do you have any of those documents here with you in court today relating to orders to units to travel to Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Your Honours, we have a 65 ter list and documents that the Prosecutor is proposing to ask questions about. Now the Prosecutor doesn't just fly blind, doesn't just make up questions as they go along. I don't know what my learned friend has in mind here. If he's referring to documents that we've got, that have been provided to us by the Prosecutor in the proper way, that's one thing. And if there are documents that we know nothing about that the Prosecutor is trying to bring into evidence, that's quite another thing. Now, I don't wish to embarrass anyone in court, well, I'll say no more about it. The Prosecutor ought to indicate what the possible relevance of these questions is and why it's being pursued in the way it has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I think that's a reasonable request. And Mr. Re, would you please clarify this matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll withdraw the question. I'll move to another area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, I want to ask you about conversations you had with Mr. Halilovic in relation to his order of the 23rd of September, that's P389. That was the order asking you to form a company of soldiers to the Vrdi front.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want to ask you about a conversation with Mr. Halilovic on the 22nd of September 1993. Were you aware whether your telephone was tapped in 1993, whether people were intercepting your telephone calls?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I say that I knew 100 per cent, the next question will be how come I knew? I don't have any firm arguments in this respect. But I can say that I did know, because, as corps commander, my conversations were monitored all the time. I became sure of that after a few situations, but I wasn't bothered by the fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about Mr. Halilovic's telephone? Were you aware whether his telephone was intercepted at the same time yours was?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't know that, but if my conversations were intercepted, as I was corps commander, then it is only logical to expect that General Sefer Halilovic's conversations were intercepted, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you know who was intercepting your telephone conversations, which organisation?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At any rate, the service of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did -- do you remember speaking to Mr. Halilovic about Caco and Celo on the 22nd of September 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not remember that specifically. I don't know what you mean actually. As I say, there were conversations, so if you remind me, I'll tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did Mr. Halilovic request to see Caco and Celo?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If my friend wants to ask leading questions, then he shouldn't, and I object to it. But Your Honours, there is another issue that has to be raised here, I'm not sure -- no, I'll wait until my learned friend goes further. But I object to that question. There is to be no leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The witness specifically asked me to remind him about a particular conversation. That's the one I want him to testify about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's still objectionable. There might have been such a conversation, there might not have been such a conversation. And it's not for my friend to give evidence from the bar table that there was such a conversation. Now, in my respectful submission, it's just a leading question and it's not permitted. Even if the witness did ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, the witness could answer no, he could say "yes," "no," "I don't know," "I don't remember."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you could ask a more general question, for instance, in the conversation, whether Caco or Celo were mentioned or something.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there a conversation between you and Mr. Halilovic in which Caco and Celo were mentioned on the 22nd of September 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is hard for me to say whether it was on the 22nd of September. Given the time distance, I cannot recall whether I had a conversation on the 22nd of September with Sefer Halilovic. I can say that I did have conversations and in these conversations those two men had been referred to. It is possible that it was on the 22nd of September, but how can I say now?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In September? After the troops returned from -- after the 9th and the 10th returned from Sarajevo, that's what I -- that's what I -- sorry, returned from Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So by then, the unit of the 2nd Independent Battalion had returned. Now, whether at that moment the companies from the 9th and 10th had returned or not is something I cannot say just off the cuff. I don't know the exact date, whether they returned by then, but it is that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did Mr. Halilovic want from you, if he indeed wanted anything from you? What did he say to you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably to have the units sent again, to speed up the process of preparing the unit, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which units?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that battalion, and its establishment had been requested. I think that in his order of the 23rd of September, there is no concretisation in terms of what unit is involved but only the number of soldiers involved, as opposed to the first order of the 2nd of September 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did he say to you when you contacted him or when he contacted you about which units he wanted to go back to Herzegovina? That is in response to his order of the 23rd of September?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Once again it's a leading question. Your Honours, in my respectful submission -- no. Actually I withdraw the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. The objection is gone. Please answer the question.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's hard for me to be precise in giving an answer. I cannot recall all the details of the conversation. It's hard.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No one expects you to. I mean, I couldn't recall it. No one here expects you to. It's the impression, it's what you remember, the impression of what he said to you. Not the exact words. No one would ever, ever ask you to say what the exact words were, unless it was extremely specific.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, your question was whether he had asked for units from the 9th and 10th again, if I understood your question correctly. I don't recall that that is exactly what he had asked for yet again. I really cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to look at a document, number 63 ter 101, which is 01471947.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI 390.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours, there is an objection to this. Your Honours, I just want it to inquire of the Prosecutor, is this what's being shown now, something that purports to be a transcript of a telephone conversation?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: It seems to me it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, at the moment, the Prosecutor would need to indicate what the source of this is, and whether the chain of custody is properly established, and who the transcript is supposed to be proved through.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have not started yet. I believe that the Prosecution will lead us to that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, well that may be so, Your Honours, but in showing the document to -- well, no perhaps you're right, Your Honour, sorry, perhaps -- Your Honour is always right. So, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to say it in those terms. I'll wait until he's read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to have a look at that document, Mr. Karavelic. It -- on its face it's a the transcript of a telephone conversation between you and Mr. Halilovic, with the date of the 22nd of September 1993. Now, what I want you to do is to look at it and to tell us whether that accords with the information -- whether the information there accords with a conversation, a telephone conversation you had with Mr. Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I object to that again. There is the same problem we had yesterday, Your Honours. If the witness doesn't bring the document into being himself, then he can't be asked to refresh his memory from it. Now, you remember my learned friend's banana submission yesterday. This is another banana, frankly, and I object to it. It's just not a possible thing to ask the witness to do, to refresh his memory from something that he didn't himself create. Perhaps he could be asked if he created this record and then we could go forward.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The objection is legally nonsense, it's nonsense. It is absolute nonsense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, well, well, well, let's not come to this argument. I believe that, first of all, you have to ask this witness to read the contents of the document. Then you ask whether that will refresh his memory that he had a conversation with Mr. Halilovic on the 22nd September 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Have you read it yet, Mr. Karavelic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, it's very hard to read this. I can just read part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Would a paper copy assist you? I can provide you with a paper copy, if it's easier to read.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. Is there a copy in English? Can I try to read it in English, if there is no Bosnian copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, while the witness is reading that, perhaps I should raise a matter of general interest about these transcripts. I'll do it in neutral terms because the witness is present. As I understand it, there is a number of transcripts the Prosecutor wants to tender. I thought that based upon indications in the past, that these transcripts would be ultimately tendered through a witness with another name, another witness, who is coming later. And it's important that there just be some consistency about it. I don't want to put the Prosecution in a difficult position now because the witness is here of course, and it's not fair to the Prosecutors to say, well, he has to wait until that witness has come to authenticate it, all these transcripts. But at the same time, it raises a real issue for us on the Defence side because we may want to object to some of these transcripts. There may be questions of the legality of how they were obtained and so on, and using transcripts like there, if they were obtained illegally, is something that the Tribunal would have -- at least be required to have some thoughts about, whether you decided to admit them in the end would be a matter for you -- for your discretion. Now, I'm not being critical of the Prosecution at all in this regard, the witness is here and they have to deal with this matter now, but the Defence also has a problem because by agreeing to or taking a stance in respect of one document, we then might --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: What is your suggestion?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, my suggestion is perhaps this little part of the -- of the cross-examination be deferred - it's only a suggestion - be deferred until the next break. It might be then that I could speak to my learned friend and another counsel from the Prosecutor who are dealing with these matters. It's not something I ask to you do now, but I think it better be raised now because otherwise to protect my position I'll have to take lengthy objections to this document, which may not be the appropriate document to do it with. I'm sorry, perhaps I'm being a bit obscure but I don't want to go into the facts with the witness here, as Your Honours might understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. In every case, there will be a dispute between the parties concerning of the so-called tapped conversations. I believe that is quite normal. My suggestion is that we go along with this witness concerning with this document, because this piece of document was a conversation between himself and Mr. Sefer Halilovic. Unless there is some evidence that this document is obtained illegally, we will allow the use of this document in the courtroom. It's applicable to all this kind of documents. As for whether we should admit it or not, we might do it all together, concerning all those intercepts in the future during which both parties are free, especially Defence, to file a submission explaining their positions in details. Is it agreeable to the parties?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, if our position is protected, that's appropriate, Your Honour. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, you've put it down, have you read the -- the English of it?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I've read the first page and a half, until the following two interlocutors. I mean, I don't think this has anything to do with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, it doesn't. Having read that, does that refresh your memory as to a conversation you had with Mr. Halilovic in which Caco and Celo were mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry, I have to repeat the objection from before. It's not appropriate to have the witness refresh his memory from a document that he didn't create. And I think I should add some legal substance to this. It's always the case in common law systems that before a witness is entitled to refresh his memory from a document, it has to be proved that he made the document, that the events were fresh in his memory at the time he made the document, that the document was -- that the information in the document was accurate, at the time, and that he has recently refreshed his memory from it. Those are the four preconditions in every common law jurisdictions, as my learned friend must know. But if there needs to be a submission filed about this we'll do that because that's clearly the law and everyone knows it. That's the first thing. It may be appropriate to get a witness to comment upon the contents of a particular document, as the witness has done. And as I've said all along no objection to him saying what he remembers, no objection to him offering - if it's appropriate to do so - a comment about something. But to try to effect his memory with a document he may never have seen, and my friend hadn't even asked him that yet, that he may never have seen is not permissible. So I object to the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I'm afraid that I could not agree with you, because during the previous testimony, this witness said that he had conversations with Mr. Sefer Halilovic during that period. The problem is that he could not remember the exact date and time, he could not remember the exact contents of that conversation. So in this way, this is the basis for the Prosecution to put this document to him, try to refresh his memory of that particular day. I don't think there is any problem on that, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I won't -- I won't -- I'll say one more thing about it, if I may, and that will be the last comment I make about it, but my objection is not to what Your Honour has raised, but it's different to that. My objection is that in assisting his memory, you can't show him something that he doesn't know if it's accurate, true or not, that he's never seen. Now the Prosecutor could ask him, have you seen this before? Is it accurate? If it is, does it refresh your memory? But to put it in front of him after 11 years when it may be, I don't know yet because the question hasn't been asked, but it may be that he's never seen this before or only recently, and he's not in a position to verify whether it's accurate or edited or any of those sort of things. He may not know. He may. If he knows, I'm finished. But if he doesn't know, it may be a matter that is of concern, and in my submission, he ought to be asked that preliminary question before we go any further. That's as far as I will add to my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Yes, of course. But the question here is not whether he has seen this document before or not. The question is whether he did that conversation or not. As you request, Mr. Re, you may ask a question about whether this witness has seen this document, I mean that piece of paper, before or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, apart from me showing it to you last week when I was proofing you, had you ever seen it before?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since there is doubt as to whether I have brought this document, I did not bring this document. I first saw it last week here when I arrived in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. What I'm asking you to do is to look at the document, I think you've read it now, and to answer this: Having read it, does it refresh your memory as to a conversation you had with Mr. Halilovic in which Caco and Celo were mentioned? You mentioned earlier in your evidence having such conversations with Mr. Halilovic. Does this particular document refresh your memory as to any conversation you had with him?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's very hard for me to be very specific, and to confirm that with any degree of certainty. I cannot say, in view of the many facts referred to in this document, that they did not take me back to that period of time, but to an equal extent, they created confusion in my mind, so it is hard for me to get things in the right order, whether it was all in that conversation or whether it was a mix, whether that was the case or whether that was not the case, it's very hard for me to say anything. Basically, I stand by what I gave by way of an answer before having read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well what do you remember about speaking to Mr. Halilovic in September 1993 after the troops came back from Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, I object to that. That was asked before. Now my friend is putting this document before him and asking it again when the witness has given a clear answer as to the effect of this document and his memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I actually wasn't. I withdraw that question because I don't want to get into another five minutes of speeches from the other side on this particular issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Karavelic, I'm asking you about conversations you had with Mr. Halilovic after the 9th and 10th came back from Jablanica or Herzegovina. I'm specifically asking you about whether Mr. Halilovic at any time requested to see any of those who had been to Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean officers or soldiers? I'm sure you mean soldiers -- I mean, I'm sure you mean officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that document is here too. I first saw it here when I came to The Hague, or was it before that? I need to be reminded on that. There is a document, I don't know the exact date, but it does say in that document when he asked for these people to come for a meeting with him, and they did go to meet him in Sarajevo. That document exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Who were the people he wanted to meet?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are talking about that document, on that document it says the commander of the 10th Brigade, the deputy commander of the 9th Brigade, and of delta and of the 2nd Independent Battalion respectively, I think that's what it says there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember Mr. Halilovic asking to meet the commander of the 10th, the deputy commander of the 9th, the commander of the delta and the commander of the 2nd Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a written document which can give you an answer to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, my question is whether you remember it. Do you remember him asking to see those people?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I do remember. I myself signed the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of document is it? Was it an order?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it's my order ordering these four officers of mine to report to General Sefer Halilovic's office for a meeting at a certain time and date as stated in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And was that after they had all returned to -- returned from Herzegovina and before Operation Trebevic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was certainly before the Trebevic operation, but I cannot say whether all of them had returned up until that point. I really don't know off the top of my head the dates when each of the units returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did General Halilovic request of you that they come -- that those four officers come and see him? Was it by telephone or in writing, or in a meeting?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember. I would need to read the document and then I could say more about -- or I could say more, give you an answer, if I could be just -- if I could see the document, then I could refresh my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is the document you're referring to an order you sent to those particular people?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just said that. I did give you an answer to that question. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And did you send orders to each of those four people to go and meet General Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, sorry, I have an objection there. There seems to be some mystery about the document here. Could I just ask the Prosecutors, are they referring to a document that they have in their possession or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, the witness mentioned there is a document first. I also have the question whether this document is in the possession of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The document is not in the possession of the Prosecution, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My question was: Did you send written orders to each of those people to go and meet General Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did those four people, to your knowledge, go and meet General Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be 100 per cent certain, but I think that they did. I wasn't informed about the outcome. I didn't receive any information about it later. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And are you saying that these orders exist in written form?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the archives of the army of the federation, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was the last time you saw these orders, Mr. Karavelic?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Often. If I signed it at the time and issued it, that was when I saw it, and also recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which orders did you recently see?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Amongst others, the ones that we are talking about now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did Mr. Halilovic want the meeting with those people to take place? Was it in his office or in some other place?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've got a matter of law I think should be raised in the absence of the witness here. I'm sorry to do this, but I think it has to be done now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Madam usher would you please show the witness out of the room for a while?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecutor is asking specific questions about documents here. The Prosecutor has got to explain what they know about these documents and where they think these documents are if they are not in their possession. We are getting indirect evidence about -- about documents. And it's very difficult for the Defence to deal with those and I don't know whether -- frankly, I don't know what the situation is with those, but I'm not in a position to be able to object I'm not in a position to get instructions. I'm not in a position to deal with these matters at the moment and I can't let it proceed any further unless something is done. So I ask the Prosecutors to indicate now where are these documents and what do they know about them, and what's the basis -- my friend must have a basis for asking these questions in quite a close way of the witness. Are there some documents here that we haven't been given, I'm not making any accusations but I need to know what the situation is in order to properly do my job, frankly. So I ask the Prosecutor to explain what the situation is with these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution has none of these documents in its possession. If it did, it would be using them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, that's not an answer, Your Honour. Where are they? That's what we need to know. I mean the Prosecutor is relying on this issue of possession. We want to know what the situation is. Why are they being questioned about them and why are things proceeding as they are in this mysterious way. I mean, because this raises issues for me, how do I cross-examine this witness about these ghostly documents? It's not an answer to say that I haven't got them. We rather guessed that they didn't have them. I think that would have been obvious. The question is, they know about them, they're questioning about them closely, so where are they?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, as I said before, that this witness himself mentioned that document and he testified about the meetings between people coming back from Jablanica with Mr. Halilovic on that day, out of his own memory. Of course, he said that there is a document, and he alleged that this document is in the archive at home. So, Mr. Re, would you please shed us more information about this document? I believe that Mr. Morrissey is eager to get hold of those documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If we could move into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, we will go to the private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And could we have the witness called back?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Karavelic. My question before our short break was: Where did Mr. Halilovic request the meeting to take place? Was it in his office or some other place?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it was in Sarajevo, in his office.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. I wish to move to another area now. If you just bear with me for one moment. Before I do, just to complete this area, did units of the 9th and 10th return to Herzegovina, to Mr. Halilovic, in late September 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I received the order of the 23rd of September that I talked about, and following my attempts to form a battalion, as it states in the order, I think I talked about that yesterday, I named the commander and the deputy commander of the battalion, Zijad and Fuad, and because of certain circumstances, I had to appoint other commanders to those duties, a few days passed and as far as I can remember, I think that the units did not go to Jablanica any more, but I am not 100 per cent certain about it, because the operation was suspended quite soon after.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You gave some evidence several days ago about the activities of the 9th and the 10th in Sarajevo in 1993. You gave some evidence about -- when a cannon was trained upon you and the 1st Mountain Brigade headquarters, when President Izetbegovic thought that Caco's men were firing at the Presidency building. You gave evidence about hearing about the surrounding of a police station, about their refusal to obey orders. What I want you to ask you about is the steps that were taken by the -- or any steps that were taken by the 1st Corps Command in 1993 to do something about what the 9th -- to do something to control the activities of the 9th and 10th.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know specifically what you're thinking of. Could you please be a little more clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. When you were the deputy commander and then the commander of the 1st Corps, what steps did the corps take to control the activities of the 9th Motorised Brigade and the 10th Mountain Brigade? You've given us evidence about their indiscipline and criminal activities. What steps were taken to -- to control these activities?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first measure that was taken was taken already in May or June. There is a document relating to that as well. I don't know if you have it or if it's in the archives of the Federation army. When the first commander of the 1st Corps, Mustafa Hajrulahovic, passed the document on requesting the replacement of a number of officers, brigade commanders and other officers, this document was sent to the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command, Sefer Halilovic, and I think that this same document was sent to the Supreme Command, and President Izetbegovic, by Sefer Halilovic. Why President Izetbegovic did not do that then, it's hard for me to say. A very similar document was also sent out by me, in an expanded form, with a number of officers and brigade commanders, including the ones that you are talking about. This was in late August or early September, when I drafted this document, and of course sent it to Rasim Delic and Rasim Delic sent it to the Supreme Command and President Izetbegovic. These were the sorts of measures that were being taken. The political leadership did not - I don't know why - take that seriously, and did not take steps to replace these people with a -- I was deeply convinced that the Supreme Command and President Izetbegovic were very well informed about these matters. We were waiting for a plan for the Trebevic operation. Why? Well, I could just give you arbitrary comments but I would rather not go into that. Other steps that were taken, many such steps, attempting to approach these people, to advise them, and to try to bring these people into the system, into a routine called military hierarchy, rules and order, the proper conduct according to military rules. I would need to look at the documents to check, but I think that there was certain disciplinary measures as well. There were also attempts, through various other subjects who could contribute to these activities, to inform these people and to use their skills, their combat abilities, and bravery, in the struggle against the aggressor rather than to dilute these skills and serve the purposes of the aggressor and take away from our own objectives.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did the commander Talijan inform the Supreme Command, Mr. Halilovic, and the Presidency of, in June of 1993?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said a lot in the document, and it would be good to have the document here to read it. The document was confirmed by Sefer Halilovic and sent to the Supreme Command, and as I said, to Alija Izetbegovic. He said a lot in the document but I don't know what he said in the conversation with them. He was the commander. I was the deputy, and I rarely had the opportunity to attend talks of Mustafa Hajrulahovic, the 1st Corps commander, with Sefer Halilovic, or the Supreme Command as a whole, or only with President Izetbegovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: After you became first -- I withdraw that. Why didn't the 1st Corps commander, Talijan, take steps, positive steps, to try and control these two brigades? That is before you assumed command at the end of July 1993.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would need a lot of time to give you a detailed, reasonable answer. The briefest response would be to ask you a question. What could he have done?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I actually wasn't there. You were. If you could give us a brief answer to the problems confronting him and why there -- why they stopped him doing anything, it would really assist.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The capital of Bosnia-Herzegovina is Sarajevo. From early April 1992, it was completely under siege. Only a bird would be able to go in and out of the city, and perhaps some individuals, but they would be exposed to fire. Throughout 1992 and 1993, and until 1995, a battle for the city was waged. The aggressor wanted to capture the town at any cost. If they managed to get into the city, and I spoke about that a little bit, what would be the -- I said what the people were thinking, including myself as deputy commander and later when I took upon the duties for which it would have been better of me not to have taken upon myself.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will -- I will come to the question, yes. Yes, here's a direct answer. In the formation of units of the 1st Corps, in the city of Sarajevo, the units - please - were not formed in accordance with any kind of mobilisation plan. The units were not formed in accordance with somebody's decisions, this soldier will go here and this soldier will go here, this officer will be a commander of a battalion, this one will be the commander of a brigade. It wasn't done like that. This was done when the system fell apart in 1992, in April 1992, and people simply formed units in their streets, in their neighbourhoods, and this is how we got the largest number of brigade commanders, battalion commanders, platoon and company commanders. Regardless of whether these people were fit to do so, whether they were mentally and physically fit to do so or not. And this is very important when we are talking about military organisation. By forming such units, which was not done in accordance with strict organisational rules and control, nobody passed any kind of testing for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, you had certain --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We are running short of time. I really do --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, no, no. This is an important question. He's entitled to answer it in the way he is. He's been asked what the problems were facing Talijan and he's entitled to give a proper answer, not to be told we're running short of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We are in April of 1992. I only want him to answer about 1993, what the problems were in 1993. For my purposes, I don't require the historical background from 1992. Mr. Morrissey is quite entitled to cross-examine on that but it's not what I'm after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Witness, I think you have to understand that Judge El Mahdi was a Judge in Galic's case. He's very familiar with the situation in Sarajevo during that time, and I was a Judge in Naletilic case and I'm very familiar with the situation in Mostar so all those background informations are not new to us. Would you please focus your answer to the question put by the Prosecution and come to that directly?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In 1993, please, we really do understand, there has been a lot of evidence about 1992. What was preventing you and your predecessor in 1993 from taking action against the 9th and the 10th, up until Trebevic? What were the problems confronting you? Why couldn't you do it? What were the obstacles?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A simple answer would be he could not, he did not have the manpower, the means, and had he dared to do so, and tried to do that, his corps would have fallen apart and Sarajevo would have fallen into the hands of the enemy. This is something that I believe 100 per cent. We can talk about it but excuse me, I'm not saying anything. If anybody says that they know the situation in Sarajevo in 1993, just because of one criminal procedure, then they are deeply deluded. I myself, who lived in Sarajevo throughout that period, and held such a high position, am only finding out about certain facts today that I was not aware of, that I did not know about, and that I did not understand. And only today am I afraid when I think back of what I did and the times that I lived through. And I'm still not quite sure how I managed to come out of it alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I note the time. It's about 10.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We'll take a break and I hope that your direct examination is approaching to its end, as you promised yesterday, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It certainly is. I'm getting very close.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Sorry, might I just mention one matter briefly before we -- my friend resumes. This is just a matter that arises out -- it may be an interpretation issue but -- I'm sorry. At page 21, line 10, the witness gave an answer in response to something that was said -- I think there was a question by the Prosecution, but then I raised some matters, I'm advised by the Bosnian speakers on our team that in the translation process, it might have appeared that the Defence was suggesting that the witness, Mr. Karavelic, had actually brought a document to The Hague, that that transcript, that telephone transcript. That wasn't our submission at the time, but the Bosnian speakers here have just pointed out that that may be how it came across. The witness gave an answer at line -- at line 10, "since there is doubt whether I have brought this document to The Hague," and we just don't want to leave any confusion for the Prosecutors or for the Bench: We are not making any such allegation at all, and if that was a mistake that occurred in translation, which frankly, I can't say anything about, but I'm told it might have, the Prosecution don't have to fight that -- nobody has to deal with it because we are not making that allegation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I believe that the translation section will have that checked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re, would you please proceed?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before the break, you were telling us about the problems in Sarajevo and the difficulties in dealing with the 9th and the 10th. What was your assessment in 1993, when you were both deputy commander and commander, of what the consequences could have been had you attempted to militarily deal with the 9th and the 10th?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This question, had it been dealt with a lot earlier, in relation to when it actually happened, from political point of view, and I am first of all speaking about the political aspect of it, because the military is only a product of the political, there could have been polarisation within the corps, a split-up into two parts at least, if not even more, two or three or even more than that. This polarisation of the corps, along political lines, would have, of course, inevitably led to consequences which belong to the military aspect. There would have been military polarisation too, which would indubitably cause mutual conflicts, including armed conflicts. This further on leads to the fact that such steps would quite simply lead to the self-destruction of the corps, the 1st Corps of the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina and in this way, the defence of Sarajevo, which would all work in favour of the aggressor. And how? Since the basic mission of the 1st Corps of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina was the mission that it was given by the command of Bosnia-Herzegovina as a political and military body, that is to say to defend the capital of Bosnia-Herzegovina at all costs. This shows that the corps commanders' intention was to preserve the internal unity of the corps at all costs to prevent internal conflicts and disputes either politically or militarily and to keep the corps facing the aggressor in order to carry out their primary mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps putting my question more directly to you, what was your assessment of what would have happened had you gone down to the brigade headquarters of the 9th or the 10th, with your military police battalion, and attempted to arrest Caco or Celo?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are now talking about the 9th and 10th, but, please, that is not the only case, the 9th and 10th. But we are talking about the 9th and 10th now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes, I want you to talk about the 9th and the 10th, not anything else.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What would happen, would ten or 50 or 100, I don't know how many casualties. That's what would happen. And now the question is: Would that be the objective of the corps commander?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your position in August and September 1993 as to what should happen to bring the 9th and the 10th under your discipline?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My position was clear: As soon as I came corps commander, which was the top position, that was in mid-1993, I said that directly and personally, in the Office of the President of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, Alija Izetbegovic, I said that to him himself: "Either make it possible for me to carry out political preparations and give me a document in writing that I can use any kind of armed force against all those who do not respect the chain of command, or simply remove me from this position that you appointed me to a month ago, or two months ago, a month or two ago."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was President Izetbegovic's response to you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He kept quiet for a long time, and then he asked me whether I seriously meant this. My answer was, "Yes," and then he said, "Wait for about 15 days" - he was not very specific as far as time was concerned - "for him to carry out political preparations." That's what he said, verbatim, and that I would get such a document in writing that would enable me to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Then what happened? You said you were waiting for a document.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was waiting, and I got this document. Political preparations were carried out. The unity of the civilian police and of my military was ensured, and we did that together on the 26th of October 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you -- you've referred to a personal conversation you had with President Izetbegovic in his office. Did you ever write to the president or Mr. Delic, the Supreme Commander, about these problems, proposing solutions?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think that when I spoke about this other document a few moments ago, when I sent when I came to the head of the 1st Corps, in that document n addition to all the names that I referred to in terms of being removed from their positions, I think that I said quite a few things about what my proposals were, and there were other documents, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you could be a little bit more specific, did you -- you said there were documents. Did you actually write to the president and Mr. Delic in relation to dismissing commanders and proposing solutions?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm saying now. That's the answer I gave a few moments ago. Yes. But I hardly ever abused the right to write to the Supreme Command or rather the president of the Presidency, although in certain situations I did that as well. It is for me to write to the commander of the staff of the Supreme Command, and it is for him to send this document further on, to the Supreme Command, either yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which commanders did you propose the dismissal of?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A larger number. I think it was between six and ten persons. I would have to be reminded. I have to have a look at the document. But at any rate I think it was the commander of the 10th Brigade, the 1st Brigade, the 2nd Brigade, the deputy commander of the 9th Brigade, the commander of delta and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you want the commander of the 2nd Brigade? Is that the commander of the 2nd Independent Motorised Brigade or a different brigade?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd Mountain Brigade of the 1st and 2nd Mountain Brigades that were between the 10th Mountain Brigade and the 9th Motorised Brigade. All of these four brigades were in the old town, in the area of the old town of the city of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why did you want the commander of the Delta Brigade dismissed?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, generally speaking, because of consistent disregard for the chain of command. As far as I can remember, even when this brigade was not within the 1st Corps, I don't know when exactly, but in the summer of 1993 it was supposed to become part of the 1st Corps organically, in line with the decision of the Supreme Command. Throughout that time, there were deviations from strict observance of the chain of command. I remember when General Sefer Halilovic was Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command, that once he took me to a meeting up there to have some of these problems resolved. He himself could not deal with their problems from that point of view. It was in that sense. They did not observe the chain of command. He did everything for them to be within the chain of command that they should not listen to politics or this person or that person. There was talk of this nature, that they are directly linked to such and such a person from political life, they are linked directly to President Izetbegovic, whoever. I remember talk like that. I'm not sure whether they were directly linked to the Supreme Command at first or were they later on linked to the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command. I'm not sure. But I know that Sefer Halilovic Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command tried to bring all of this into order. Now, later, they -- or rather that brigade became an organic part of my corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you can answer this simply, please do so. Who did you regard them as reporting to? That's the 2nd -- sorry, the Delta Brigade. You said they weren't within the chain of command. Who were they reporting to?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they became an organic part of the 1st Corps they were supposed to report to me, or if they became part of it before I came to head the 1st Corps, then to the commander of the 1st Corps. My predecessor. Until then, or rather before that, who they reported to is something that I don't want to go into because I have not studied this. I may make a mistake. I don't know who it was that they reported to.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: After you became the corps commander and you wanted to have them dismissed, who did you regard them as reporting to if they weren't reporting to you?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was quite clear a few moments ago. When they became an organic part of the 1st Corps when they were placed within the 1st Corps, then they reported the same way the commander of the 10th Mountain Brigade did, to the commander of the 1st Corps but that was not consistent. That was not the way other brigades did this.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown P217? While that document is coming, when was it that you wrote to Delic and Izetbegovic proposing the dismissal of these commanders? Was it after the soldiers had gone to Herzegovina or before? Or putting it another way, how long was it before Operation Trebevic was carried out?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date of the document. I'd have to see the document, if you have it. Is it a secret? Is it not a secret?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, personally, I don't have the document but I'm asking you from your memory, not for a precise date but approximately when you sent it in relation to Trebevic.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I took over the command of the 1st Corps in mid-August, it was around that date, perhaps just before the operation or the beginning of the operation, or during the Neretva operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You have that document there now on the screen in front of you. It's a 1st Corps Command security document signed by Sacir Arnautovic of the 7th of October 1993. What I want you to do is to look -- first of all, had you seen this particular document before coming to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want you to have a look through the document and comment, based upon your own knowledge as the 1st Corps commander and what you'd seen, heard, and been told, comment on the accuracy of the information in that document. If it's -- if it's quicker to look at it I can give you a paper copy of the whole document, because I think there is about ten pages.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I first saw this document here now when I came to The Hague. I read the content of this document. I believe that the order that we talked about an hour ago, my order -- I mean that's why I mentioned that order of mine, and I lost sight of this document, which I had a look at here. That order of mine that we discussed when I wrote the order that I should send a certain number of officers to this meeting with Sefer Halilovic, it does correspond with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You're referring, are you, to the first two pages of that document, which is the -- appears to be the -- or the report or letter part which attaches a much lengthier document?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the first page of this document, which is on the screen now. As for these ten or so pages here, they speak of the report of the security service about the alleged criminal activities of Ramiz Delalic, Celo, for the most part, and Musan Topalovic, Caco.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Based upon your knowledge, the reports you had received at the time, your own sources of information, your own observations, I just want you to comment on the accuracy of the -- those ten or so pages, which is headed "information".

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, I can take it through him line by line or I can ask him to do it generally, and the quickest way is to ask him to look at it generally and to comments on whether it's accurate and if there are any inaccuracies to point out those which he -- he knows?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I object to that. If the -- if he's being asked to -- it's again it's something I've complained about before, that the witness can be asked, simply, what did he know? Then, he could be asked to comment on specific things if it's within his knowledge, but to be asked generally, "Is that accurate?" when it's ten pages worth is just going to produce a meaningless answer and nor is it appropriate to say are there any inaccuracies. What might be more appropriate to say is there anything accurate in there that he's prepared to say is accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's a fair compromise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Looking at that document, is there anything there that based upon your knowledge and experience about what happened and what Celo and Caco were up to that are accurate?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read this document last week, the entire document, if I may say so. Perhaps I skimmed through some of the lines a bit quickly, but to confirm this entire document, and the content of all these pages, all of them that are here -- how many are there? 12? No. 13 pages. I cannot confirm that. I cannot confirm many allegations made here in this document. I must admit that it was the first time I heard of some of these allegations at all when I first read this document. However, on the other hand, I must say --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just wants you could confirm those which are accurate, that's all?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, no, look.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We are going to be is a very long time if we are going to have these sorts of explanations. I just want to know it is accurate this is accurate, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: At least allow the witness to finish his answer. But the witness has to be as concise as possible.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I also must say it's hard for me to say the percentage of the perhaps 10, 20, 30 per cent, 10 or 20 per cent of all of these allegations in this document, I can say that I heard of them, that they came to me through other channels, and that I informed my superior command about that. However, and I will finish with this, I also must say that in all of my attempts to really prove anything of what is alleged here in the document about Caco and Celo, my security service was not able to initiate proceedings or verify anything, whether it was not able to do so or whether this was not possible for some other reasons or because this information is false or wrong, it's very difficult for me to give you the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Re, it seems to me that this witness could not assist us, at least for this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: He might be able to if he went through it but I'm not going to waste the Trial Chamber's time by asking him to go through it bearing in mind the time constraints we have. In my submission it would certainly help if he told us which of the percentage -- which ones in there he thought were or he'd heard of before, but if the Trial Chamber is against me on that, in the interests of conserving time, I won't -- I won't attempt to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, the Prosecutor has the full right to ask the questions he wants to ask, if he persists with a question and asks Your Honour for permission to go on, he can do that. But the witness did give a full answer and it's the risk that the Prosecutor takes when he shows documents like this to the witness that he gets the sort of answer that he got. That's the danger of doing this, and it's not useful in my submission for that concluding speech to be made, that he doesn't want to go on with time. If he wants to get something out of that, it's up to him to do so. Not to say he's stopping because of time. It's up to the Prosecutor to either do that, or seek to do it or not to do it. And Your Honours the reason I intervened in that way is because at a later time I don't want it to be said in submissions that he could have explored this more but chose not to for time purposes. Either he explores it or doesn't explore it, in my submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Re, I think if this is your case, I believe that you have the right to do anything possible to present your case.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Karavelic, I just want you to look at it, and you said some of it was accurate or you'd heard of it before, just point out the bits in the document --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It has to be pointed out that he didn't say it was accurate. He said that he'd heard of it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That you'd heard of before.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first ten lines in the document is something that I am more or less aware of. I had heard about that. However, if you're asking me if that is so, 100 per cent, I cannot confirm it. I would be putting myself in the position of judging this. It's very hard for me to confirm that all of this is 100 per cent as it states here. There is something of this here, to a minor extent, but it's not like this, 100 per cent. The middle part of the first page, talking about racketeering, and about the cooperation of Ramiz Delalic and Musan Topalovic, Celo and Caco. I also heard and got information from other channels. However, this is just information. Whether people who had been subjected to the racketeering did not dare or did not want to confirm it, or perhaps that these allegations are true or not true, it's something that I really cannot say. This last part on the first page, I can say nothing about.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Over the page there are a number of specific incidents with specific dates. All I want you to do is just day say the date, whether you'd heard of it, the date, whether you'd heard of it, the date, whether you'd heard of it, if you could make a comment. The first is the 9th of September 1992 and so on.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 9th of September, I did not hear -- I did not hear about this, these allegations that pertain to the 9th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Next one, 29th of September.

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 29th of September is also something that I cannot confirm but something is there vaguely in my thoughts about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The 2nd of October 1992?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: 8th of October --

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 8th of October 1992, I cannot confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The 12th?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 12th of October 1992, also I cannot confirm it. The 15th of October 1992, I cannot confirm that either. The 16th of October 1992, I cannot confirm that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you say cannot confirm, do you mean you hadn't heard of it?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I hadn't heard of it, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next one is the 21st of December, 1992, raid on Markale market, seizure of 3.815 Deutschmarks?

utterances.speaker: VAHID KARAVELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps this is in that context but here it is stated specifically how much money and that it was at Markale.
